feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so it states no outcome for it. Evidence: iteration 0 and 4 (wheel_track 0.12 m, five sensors, kp 4.0, mass 0.6 kg) scored 96.84, with s-bend max_error 0.0703 m, line loss 2, and steering_oscillation 0.2533. Iteration 5 (wheel_track 0.10 m, kp 4.0, otherwise unchanged) scored 112.54, with oval progress up from 0.43 to 0.55, s-bend max_error 0.0626 m, and oval oscillation 0.277, above the 0.25 caution level. Iterations 2 and 3 lowered the score when track width, mass, footprint and look-ahead changed together, so those drops cannot be assigned to track width alone. Your 0.09 m track gives about 11 percent more yaw per command than iteration 5, so I lowered kp to 3.5 in the controller to keep kp / wheel_track near iteration 5's level. Next race: if the score is above 112.54 and oval oscillation stays below about 0.25, keep wheel_track at 0.09 m and try 0.08 m only if s-bend max_error is still above 0.06 m. If oval steering_oscillation is still above 0.25, the controller is the limit, not the geometry, so keep 0.09 m and lower kp, rather than widening the track. If the score falls below 112.54, revert wheel_track to 0.10 m.
requested_changes: If s-bend max_error is still above 0.06 m with steering_oscillation below about 0.25 and the score above 112.54: propose wheel_track 0.08 m, citing iteration 5's s-bend max_error improvement from 0.0703 to 0.0626 m.
If the score falls below 112.54: revert wheel_track to 0.10 m, citing iteration 5 as the best-supported geometry, and keep the five-sensor layout and 0.6 kg mass.

If oval steering_oscillation exceeds 0.25 at 0.09 m: keep wheel_track at 0.09 m and do not change the sensor array, citing iteration 5's oscillation of 0.277 as evidence that the yaw gain, not the sensing, is the limit.
